spatial_claims.claim: D lies on line AG such that AG = AD + DG; DG is the annex to the first apotome AD
E bisects DG, so E is the midpoint of segment DG
H lies on segment AG such that AH x HG = EG squared (application of area deficient by a square)
AD = AG - GD, so AC x AD = AC x AG - AC x GD (area decomposition along a line)
p squared + q squared = AC x (AH + HG) = AC x AG (additive area decomposition along segment AG)
pq = AC x EG, so 2pq = AC x GD (using AH x HG = EG squared and E bisects DG)
(p - q) squared = p squared + q squared - 2pq = AC x AD = area AB (algebraic identity 2.7)

configuration_map: All constructed points lie on a single straight line. The approximate order is A...H...D...E...G, where: AG is the whole rational line, DG is the annex to the first apotome AD, E is the midpoint of DG, and H is determined on segment AG by the condition AH x HG = EG squared. The auxiliary magnitudes p and q are defined purely algebraically by p squared = AC x AH and q squared = AC x HG. The entire proof operates through commensurability relationships and area algebra with no multi-dimensional spatial configuration.
skip_reason: The proof is purely algebraic/proportional, dealing with commensurability and incommensurability of straight lines and areas (rational vs. medial). All geometric elements are points on a single line and rectangle area computations. There are no triangle interior/exterior claims, no angle decompositions, no ray betweenness claims, and no circle configurations. This is characteristic of Book 10 irrational magnitude theory, which is algebraic rather than spatial in nature.
